1.title: The Continual Improvement Model
1.text: Welcome to Module eleven: The Continual Improvement Model. It covers the exam area The eye til Value System. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do four things. List the steps of the eye til Continual Improvement Model. Understand each step. Describe continual improvement within the eye til Value System and its role in the organization. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: The eye til Value System (forty percent). Exam format: forty multiple-choice questions in sixty minutes; twenty-six correct answers (sixty-five percent) pass. Validated against: the official eye til Foundation (Version five) syllabus, version five point zero (February two thousand twenty-six).

1.title: Why a model
1.text: Why a model. Continual improvement is a recurring activity at all levels, from the whole organization to a single practice. The eye til Continual Improvement Model gives a repeatable path for each improvement: from vision to evaluated results. It supports the guiding principles (especially progress iteratively with feedback) and is the fifth component of the eye til Value System.

1.title: The seven steps
1.text: The seven steps. Each step asks a question. one. Step: Vision. Question: What is the vision? two. Step: Current state. Question: Where are we now? three. Step: Target state. Question: Where do we want to be? four. Step: How to get there. Question: How do we get there? (the plan). five. Step: Action. Question: Take action. six. Step: Evaluation. Question: Did we get there? seven. Step: Momentum. Question: How do we keep the momentum going?

1.title: The seven steps, continued
1.text: The seven steps. The figure shows this: The seven steps of the continual improvement model, with the loop back to the start.

1.title: The seven steps, continued
1.text: The seven steps. The model is described as a refined version of the eye til four model; the seven steps and their order match the eye til four model. Check the official book for exact wording. Exam tip: Vision, where are we, where do we want to be, how do we get there, take action, did we get there, keep momentum. The model is a loop: after step seven the work continues.

1.title: Key points on each step
1.text: Key points on each step. Vision. Link to the organization's vision and objectives, so improvement serves value. Current state. Measure the baseline; start where you are. Target state. Set a clear, measurable goal. How to get there. Plan small, achievable steps; use iteration. Action. Do the work, collaborate, keep it visible. Evaluation. Check results against the target; learn from feedback. Momentum. Embed the change, celebrate, and choose the next improvement.

1.title: Role in the ITIL Value System
1.text: Role in the eye til Value System. Continual improvement touches every other component: it improves the practices, the value chain activities, governance and the application of the principles. It is not a project that ends; it is part of everyday work for everyone. Exam tip: The steps are questions you can ask in order: vision, now, target, plan, act, evaluate, keep going. A scenario that checks results against the target is evaluation, not action. Exam tip: The model is a loop, not a project plan. An option that says improvement stops after the action step, or happens only once, is wrong.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Which is the correct order of the first three steps of the continual improvement model? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Vision, current state, target state. The order is vision, current state, target state.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A team has measured its baseline and now asks where it wants to be. Which step is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Target state. Setting the goal is the target state step.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Which statement about the continual improvement model is C O R R E C T? (one) It has seven steps. (two) It ends once the action step is complete. (three) The evaluation step asks whether the target was reached. (four) Momentum is the first step. The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: one and three. The model has seven steps, and evaluation checks whether the target was reached.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Identify the missing word(s). The last step of the continual improvement model asks how to keep the blank going. The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Momentum. The final step is about keeping the momentum going.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. After a new process went live, the team compared results with the target and gathered feedback. Which step is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Evaluation. Checking whether the target was reached is evaluation.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which statement best describes continual improvement in the eye til Value System? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: A recurring activity that applies at all levels and improves every other component. Continual improvement is part of everyday work and touches every component.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. How many steps are in the continual improvement model? Answer: Seven. Question two. What question does the "current state" step ask? Answer: Where are we now? Question three. Which step asks "Did we get there?". Answer: Evaluation.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What is the last step? Answer: Momentum: how do we keep the momentum going? Question five. Which guiding principle does the model support most directly? Answer: Progress iteratively with feedback. Question six. Is continual improvement a one-time project? Answer: No; it is a recurring activity at all levels.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Seven steps: vision, current state, target state, how to get there, action, evaluation, momentum. Shape: a loop; improvement continues. Role: fifth component; improves all the others. Old wording: the eye til four model has the same seven steps.
